# API & Contract Requirements Checklist: Taskify Kanban Board

**Purpose**: Validate the requirements quality of the REST and WebSocket contracts
(`contracts/rest-api.md`, `contracts/websocket-events.md`) drafted in the planning
phase — completeness, clarity, consistency with spec.md — ahead of implementation.
**Created**: 2026-10-29
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [contracts/rest-api.md](../contracts/rest-api.md) · [contracts/websocket-events.md](../contracts/websocket-events.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Is the distinction between a missing `X-User-Id` header and an unknown/invalid one addressed, or does the contract only define the "unknown id → 401" case? [Gap, contracts/rest-api.md §Base path]
- [x] CHK002 When a single `PATCH /api/tasks/:taskId` request carries both `status` and `assigneeUserId` and the status change is blocked by FR-008, is the outcome for the assignee change (applied vs rejected along with it) specified? [Gap, contracts/rest-api.md §Tasks]
- [x] CHK003 Is an API versioning strategy (or an explicit statement that none is needed for this phase) documented anywhere in the contracts? [Gap]
- [x] CHK004 Is duplicate-submission/idempotency behavior specified for `POST /api/projects` and `POST /api/projects/:projectId/tasks` (e.g., a double-click producing two identical projects/tasks)? [Gap, contracts/rest-api.md §Projects, §Tasks]
- [x] CHK005 Are pagination or page-size limits specified for `GET /api/projects` and `GET /api/projects/:projectId/tasks` as project/task counts grow beyond the 3 seeded projects? [Gap, contracts/rest-api.md]
- [x] CHK006 Is the server's behavior documented for a `join:project` request naming a `projectId` that doesn't exist (error ack shape), or only the success path? [Gap, contracts/websocket-events.md §Connection lifecycle]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK007 Is the `since` query parameter's timestamp format (precision, timezone) quantified beyond "ISO timestamp", so two implementations couldn't interpret it differently? [Clarity, Ambiguity, contracts/rest-api.md §Notifications]
- [x] CHK008 Is "the most recent N" (when `since` is omitted on the notifications endpoint) given a concrete value for N? [Clarity, Ambiguity, contracts/rest-api.md §Notifications]
- [x] CHK009 Is the `error` field in the `{ "error", "message" }` response shape defined as a stable, enumerable code, or left as free text indistinguishable between failure reasons (e.g., two different 403s)? [Clarity, contracts/rest-api.md §Base path]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK010 Is the CORS restriction described in tasks.md (T058, frontend-origin-only) reflected as a requirement in `contracts/rest-api.md` itself, or does it exist only in the task list? [Consistency, Gap]
- [x] CHK011 Does the contract's comment-text validation ("empty text" per FR-013) explicitly state whether whitespace-only text is treated as empty, consistent with the same open question already raised against the spec (task-rules.md CHK007)? [Consistency, contracts/rest-api.md §Comments]
- [x] CHK012 Is the WebSocket contract's implicit rule — any of the 5 users may join any project's room with no membership check — cross-referenced to the spec's "single shared workspace" assumption, so a reader doesn't need to infer it independently? [Consistency, contracts/websocket-events.md §Connection lifecycle]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK013 Is a concurrency-control mechanism (e.g., version/ETag) specified for `PATCH /api/tasks/:taskId`, or does the contract rely silently on database write ordering to satisfy the spec's "last update applied wins" edge case? [Edge Case, Gap, contracts/rest-api.md §Tasks]
- [x] CHK014 Does `POST /api/projects/:projectId/tasks` specify the error response when the optional `assigneeUserId` refers to a non-existent user? [Edge Case, Gap, contracts/rest-api.md §Tasks]
- [x] CHK015 Does `PATCH /api/tasks/:taskId` specify the error response when `assigneeUserId` refers to a non-existent user, distinct from the "unassign via null" case? [Edge Case, Gap, contracts/rest-api.md §Tasks]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK016 Are rate-limiting or throttling requirements specified for the unauthenticated REST endpoints, given the plan's trusted-network-only constraint? [Gap, Non-Functional]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK017 Is the dependency between the WebSocket `join:project` ack's task-list payload and the `GET /api/projects/:projectId/tasks` response shape documented as "must stay identical," so a future change to one contract doesn't silently desync the other? [Traceability, Dependency, contracts/websocket-events.md §Connection lifecycle]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK018 Is there any remaining ambiguity in who may initiate `leave:project` — only the user who joined, or can any client request any room be left — given no per-connection ownership check is described? [Ambiguity, contracts/websocket-events.md §Client → server events]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
